VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) – User Guide, Volume 1, Specifications
The VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) provides settlement functions for the BASE II System and for
the Single Message System (SMS), including Interlink. Clients and processors get settlement
information in a standardized set of reports using common business-oriented terminology. VSS
provides flexibility in defining financial relationships, selecting reports and report destinations, and
Visa processes interchange transactions for SMS (including Interlink) and BASE II through separate
systems. SMS and BASE II perform their own clearing functions and VSS performs the settlement
functions for SMS and BASE II.
Clearing is the process of collecting an individual transaction from one client or processor
Settlement is the process of calculating and determining the net financial position of each
client for all transactions that are cleared.

VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) – User Guide, Volume 1, Specifications
Visa offers several settlement services options.
International Settlement Service—Used to settle all international transactions and
domestic transactions for clients that do not participate in a National Net Settlement Service
National Net Settlement Service (NNSS)—Allows clients within a country to settle
qualifying domestic transactions through a central settlement agent bank. Qualifying
transactions are those in which the merchant, acquirer, and issuer are in the same country.
Also, the transaction currency must be the local currency for that country for the transaction
Area Net Settlement Service (ANSS)—Allows clients within a defined area to settle
qualifying domestic transactions through a central settlement agent bank. Qualifying
transactions are those in which the merchant, acquirer, and issuer are in the same defined
area. Also, the transaction currency is the local currency for that defined area for the
Visa also offers intraday settlement for countries with an NNSS or ANSS. Intraday settlement
supports mutliple settlement windows and facilitates delivery of settlement reports, interchange
clearing files, and funds transfer instructions multiple times a day.
VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) provides a variety of capabilities to clients.
Settlement relationships—VSS provides flexibility when defining settlement relationships.
Clients can define from two to eight levels of settlement relationships. The different levels
allow them to build and maintain the most appropriate settlement relationships for their
business needs. For example, the settlement relationship levels can be used to reflect the
products in a client's organization. As such, clients can easily and efficiently manage
Report layouts and formats—VSS reports provide a common layout for BASE II- and SMS-
cleared clients, allowing them to streamline their internal procedures. All VSS reports are
available in print-ready and machine-readable formats. VSS reports use business-oriented
terminology to better reflect the business needs of clients.
Report delivery options—Clients can have their reports sent to multiple locations, including
locations other than their processing centers. Interchange routing does not determine the
Funds transfer points—The funds transfer point can be defined at any level in the
settlement structure. This flexibility allows clients using third-party processors to be
responsible for their own funds transfer.
VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) – User Guide, Volume 1, Specifications
Alternately routed and split-routed transactions—Clients can use an alternate processor,
such as Visa Exceptions, to collect and deliver (switching) selected transactions. This option is
called alternate routing for SMS and split routing for BASE II. Clients can also specify how
they want to settle their alternately-routed or split-routed transactions, electing to settle
these transactions with their normally routed transactions or separately.
National Settlement cutoff time—National Net Settlement Service (NNSS) or Area Net
Settlement Service (ANSS) clients have the option to settle domestic activity at a time that is
appropriate to their business day. The specific settlement time can be different from the
International Settlement Service cutoff time. To use this feature, all clients participating in a
particular NNSS or ANSS must agree on a common settlement cutoff time.

These terms help define a lowest-level SRE:
Clearing Entity—The entity used by the clearing systems to determine processing rules. In

Network—For Visa and VisaNet, the network is the telecommunications facility used for
message switching. For other card program networks (for example, Plus and Interlink), the
network dictates the product rules under which a transaction is processed.

International Settlement Service (the most commonly used settlement service) or through a

calculated, they are included in the total amount posted to the cardholder's account. This amount, which is in the clearing currency, is

The amount posted to the cardholder's account is a combination of:
Currency conversion fee charged by Visa.
Optional issuer fee charged by the issuer. If the issuer does not charge an optional issuer fee, this amount is 0 (zero).
The VSS–210 report shows these amounts in the cardholder billing currency (clearing currency).
The interchange amount and the currency conversion fee charged by Visa are collected in the issuer's settlement currency, so they must also
be reported in that settlement currency. This reporting allows balancing between the Visa Charges Report (VSS–140), which includes the
currency conversion fee in settlement currency, and the VSS–210 report. The optional issuer fee is not included in the settlement amount.
If a client supports multiple cardholder billing currencies for an SRE, the VSS–210 report provides amounts in settlement currency
subtotaled by clearing currency. The VSS–140 does not provide settlement subtotals by clearing currency. The subtotals in settlement
currency on the VSS–210 report should be totaled to get the total currency conversion fees shown on the VSS–140 report. See VisaNet
Settlement Service (VSS) User Guide, Volume 2, Reports.
